title: The April-March temperature difference reduced later errors for birch and beech leaf date gaps in two Swiss regions, 2011-2025
abstract: We tested whether the April-minus-March temperature difference adds information about the gap between birch and beech leaf dates beyond the March-April mean. We used 2,615 paired station-years at 104 Swiss stations. Four separate region and period fits gave negative gap slopes of -0.86 to -1.86 days per C of the temperature difference. All four station and year cluster family intervals were below zero. Three-year block intervals included zero in three of the four family tests. Fits trained on 1996-2010 reduced 2011-2025 root mean square error by 13.6% in both regions when the monthly difference was added. Two-region family intervals for this gain were 4.2-19.6% in the East and 3.3-21.5% in the West, conditional on the frozen training fits. Without a time trend, gains were 7.3% and 5.7%. Seven-day reporting-delay bounds permit either slope sign in all four samples. The regions share much of their weather. April weather often follows leaf unfolding. Thus the result supports a monthly term in later-year estimates with known weather; it does not establish a causal climate effect, a real-time forecast, or ecological harm. Missing visits, selected records, coarse weather and one observation network limit wider use. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a retrieval method and independent numerical checks are included.

display.caption: Four gap slopes and two later-year error comparisons. Blue intervals use station and year clusters. Orange intervals use three-year blocks and station resampling. Both sets allow for four slope tests. Bars on the right show point RMSE; the table gives conditional confidence intervals. The regions use separate stations but share much of their weather.

Sharp slope bounds when each reported date may follow its true date by any delay from zero to seven days. Errors can differ across species and records. All four bounds include zero. These are fixed-record possibility bounds, not confidence intervals. Actual visit intervals are absent.

citations.reason: The prior Swiss matched-event study tests winter and spring means for hazel flowering and beech leaf unfolding. We test monthly differences for two leaf events and later-year transfer. Some beech records and all weather sources overlap.

The prior beech-maple study uses actual visit brackets in two New England forests. It informs the distinction between observed visit bounds and the hypothetical delay bounds used here. We do not reuse its records or claim a new bound formula.
Prior work reports species differences in the relevant spring temperature months. It motivates, but does not validate, our Swiss transfer test.
Prior work on leaf-out synchrony and species differences motivates the question. Our signed species gap is not the within-species synchrony measure in that study.
